items.title: GET /api/scans 500s because the strict response model rejects legacy Firestore records
items.description: FOUND ONLY BY DEPLOYING. The sprint 3 revision returned HTTP 500 {code: internal_error} for GET /api/scans against real Firestore. Cloud Run logs show fastapi.exceptions.ResponseValidationError: 14 validation errors. Cause: TASK-026 declared ScanHistoryResponse.scans as list[AnalysisResponse], requiring all ten canonical fields, but hotspot_scans still holds documents written by the pre-sprint-2 broken revision - the one that persisted an un-awaited coroutine (BUG-007) and reports lacking zone_id, coordinates and alert_dispatched. One malformed historical row failed the entire request. Mocked tests never caught it because every fixture was a well-formed current-schema report. FIXED: scans is now list[dict]; history is data of mixed vintage and must degrade per row, not wholesale. /api/analyze keeps its strict model because that payload is freshly generated.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/scans returns 200 against a collection containing legacy records
POST /api/analyze keeps its strict response model
a regression test covers a legacy record missing required fields

items.title: Require local-container smoke evidence before validation handoff
items.description: Sprint 3 R1; FR-19/21/24, NFR-8/9. Establish the mandatory phase-7-to-8 smoke handoff. Sprint 4 human quota constraint overrides live deployment: prove deployability locally using backend/ build context, build/run the final image and smoke actual HTTP routes against that local container with all cloud client boundaries mocked. Reuse pipeline-smoke-test workflow, but its current live default is prohibited; provide an explicit offline-container mode with fail-closed cloud access, no ADC/.env mounts and isolated credential-free fixtures. This process task establishes the gate before implementation acceptance, not a dependency on STORY-016; final execution waits for all sprint changes and QA. Cloud-deployer owns local image execution, QA owns offline fixtures, contract-auditor owns payload/handoff validation. STORY-016 retains future cloud verification/rollback ownership and remains deferred. No .github/docs edits, gcloud calls, cloud deploys or live cloud service calls.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 7 for sprint 4 requires docker build -f backend/Dockerfile backend, a run of the resulting final image, and recorded source revision, image ID/digest, build/run commands, local URL and smoke artefact paths; no Cloud Run revision or traffic change is required.

Against the actual local container, credential-free mocked cloud boundaries demonstrate GET /api/live and /api/health, a schema-valid POST /api/analyze with caller temperature, GET /api/scans containing persisted current and legacy-shaped offline fixtures, and unsupported-upload HTTP 415; outbound cloud access fails closed.

A failed smoke check blocks validation handoff with a correctly parented defect; skipped live-cloud checks are recorded not run/unverified, never passed; local-container evidence satisfies sprint 4 acceptance.

The existing smoke workflow gains an explicit offline-container path which does not invoke doctor, verify_setup, seed upload or the live smoke default, mount credentials, or call Gemini/BigQuery/Firestore/Pub/Sub; execution is delegated to cloud-deployer, QA and contract-auditor, while STORY-016 rollback remains deferred.

items.title: Retire legacy manual smoke scripts after migrating unique checks
items.description: Sprint 4 QA retirement recommendation; FR-24/25, NFR-7/9. backend/test_analyzer.py and backend/test_pipeline.py caused cross-layer gate, coverage-denominator and schema drift for three consecutive sprints. acceptance_criteria: Unique checks from both manual scripts are inventoried and mapped to existing automated checks or the opt-in smoke workflow; no unique coverage is lost.
Human explicitly approves deletion of backend/test_analyzer.py and backend/test_pipeline.py before either file is removed.
After approval and migration both legacy scripts are removed, references are updated, and offline suite plus cross-layer and coverage-accounting checks pass without cloud calls.

items.title: Cloud Run deploy script could never have produced a working revision
items.description: Found in sprint 7 when the human asked for a redeploy. .github/skills/cloudrun-deploy/scripts/deploy.sh carried four independent defects, each fatal on its own, and none detectable by the offline suite because no test executes the deploy script. (1) Build context was the repository root while the Dockerfile's COPY paths moved to backend/ in sprint 3 — the documented triage symptom in the skill's own table, contradicted by the script three sections below it. (2) GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY and BIGQUERY_LOCATION were never passed to Cloud Run, so every sprint 6 coordinate analysis would have returned 502 in production while passing locally. (3) Default SERVICE_NAME was hotspot-sentinels but the live service is hotspot-backend, so a deploy would have created a second service instead of a new revision. (4) No --platform pin, so an arm64 host would push an image Cloud Run refuses with 'Container manifest type must support amd64/linux'. A latent fifth issue was fixed alongside: --set-env-vars used comma separation, which would have mis-parsed a multi-origin ALLOWED_ORIGINS; it now uses the ^@^ delimiter. This is the fourth recurrence of the documentation-drift class and the first where the drift was in executable code rather than prose.
acceptance_criteria: deploy.sh builds with backend/ as context, pins linux/amd64, defaults to the hotspot-backend service, and injects GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY and BIGQUERY_LOCATION.
The script aborts with a clear message when GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is unset rather than shipping a revision that 502s on coordinate analysis.
Skill prose and the triage table agree with the script on service name, build context and required runtime variables.
A real revision is deployed and verified end to end from the deployed URL.

items.title: Deployed frontend has been down since the sprint 4 dependency split
items.description: Found in sprint 7 while verifying the deployed stack for submission. https://hotspot-frontend-...run.app returned HTTP 503 and revision hotspot-frontend-00002-zk9 had NO environment variables set at all. Two independent causes. (1) The service was deployed with buildpacks, which detected a generic Python app and booted it under gunicorn as a WSGI app; Streamlit is not WSGI, so the worker could never start. (2) The revision crashed on 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named streamlit' because sprint 4's TASK-032 moved streamlit into a frontend dependency group and the default export stopped carrying it. Separately, API_BASE_URL was never set, so even a booting container would have called http://localhost:8080 inside its own sandbox and reached nothing. This was invisible for three sprints because every container proof targeted backend/Dockerfile and no check ever exercised the deployed frontend URL. Fixed by giving the frontend the same hardened multi-stage treatment as the backend: frontend/Dockerfile, frontend/.dockerignore and a frontend/requirements.txt generated by 'uv export --locked --no-hashes --only-group frontend'. Verified locally (non-root uid 10001, injected PORT honoured, /_stcore/health ok) then deployed as hotspot-frontend-00003-h56 with API_BASE_URL set, and exercised end to end in a browser: a coordinate run rendered real Maps imagery and persisted HVI 1.5 LOW for 1.3521/103.8198.
acceptance_criteria: The frontend deploys from a committed Dockerfile rather than buildpack detection, and starts Streamlit rather than gunicorn.
The frontend image installs the frontend dependency group so streamlit is present.
The deployed revision sets API_BASE_URL to the live backend and the dashboard completes a coordinate analysis end to end.
The deployed frontend URL returns HTTP 200 and /_stcore/health reports ok.

items.title: Put the codebase under version control before the submission deadline
items.description: Found in sprint 7 while checking TASK-006's 'repository shared with no secrets in history' criterion. The repository has ZERO commits and no remote: git rev-list --all --count returns 0. Seven sprints of work exist only as an uncommitted working tree on one machine, with the submission deadline on 2026-10-11. There is no history to secret-scan, no way to roll back a bad edit, and no artefact to share. The good news is that a zero-commit history is the safest possible starting point: .env has never been committed, so an initial commit made with the current .gitignore cannot leak it. Verify .gitignore covers .env, venv/, data_samples/ and __pycache__/ BEFORE the first commit, confirm git status shows no credential files staged, then commit and push. Do not use git add -A without reviewing the staged list.
acceptance_criteria: git check-ignore confirms .env, .venv/ and any key files are ignored before the first commit is created.
The staged file list is reviewed explicitly; no .env, credential, key or token file is included.
An initial commit exists and is pushed to a GitHub or Google-provided remote.
A secret scan of the pushed history finds no credential, and .env.example remains the only committed environment template.

items.title: Choose demo coordinates that show a critical hotspot
items.description: Found in sprint 7 during live demo verification; closed 2026-10-04. The old Singapore default 1.3521/103.8198 resolves at zoom 19 to dense tree canopy and correctly scores HVI 1.5 LOW — a weak opening frame for a 3-minute urban-heat recording. Five coordinates were probed against the deployed backend and all are now shipped in frontend/app.py CITY_COORDINATES: Singapore Port Terminal 1.2897/103.7540 scored CRITICAL 8.7 (100 percent asphalt, zero canopy) and is the opener; Singapore Urban Core 1.3343/103.8563 HIGH 6.6; Singapore Botanic Gardens 1.3521/103.8198 LOW 1.5 as the deliberate contrast; Bangkok City Centre HIGH 7.0; Delhi Karol Bagh HIGH 7.2. Scores reproduced identically on a second run, and the opener published a real Pub/Sub alert (alert_attempted and alert_dispatched both true, banner reads 'CRITICAL HEAT RISK: Automated Pub/Sub alert dispatched. Published successfully.'). The opening coordinate now follows the first entry of the map instead of a hardcoded key. IMPORTANT DEMO CONFIGURATION: the imagery cache is per-process (see TASK-047), and with maxScale 3 the dashboard's follow-up GET /api/imagery could land on an instance that never fetched the image, producing the attribution-unavailable error after a successful analysis. Ten consecutive 502s were observed this way. The backend was therefore pinned with 'gcloud run services update hotspot-backend --region asia-southeast1 --max-instances=1' (revision hotspot-backend-00006-8ds), after which all three Singapore coordinates serve cached imagery at 200 consistently. That pin is a demo-time setting, not a production one; TASK-046 remains the real fix.
acceptance_criteria: Demo coordinates are chosen that reliably produce a HIGH or CRITICAL risk level.
At least one scripted scenario exercises the critical alert path end to end.
The chosen coordinates are pre-warmed in the imagery cache before recording.
A contrasting low-risk location remains available to show the score responding to real surface differences.

items.title: Cover the deploy script with an offline lint so deploy drift fails the build
items.description: Raised by BUG-025. Four fatal defects sat in deploy.sh undetected because the offline suite never inspects it. A static test can catch every one of them without touching cloud: assert the docker build line uses backend/ as context and pins linux/amd64, assert the --set-env-vars string carries every variable the backend reads via os.getenv at import time, and assert the service name matches the one the verify and rollback sections of the skill document. This is the executable-drift analogue of tests/test_cross_layer_contract.py and should fail the build the same way.
acceptance_criteria: An offline test parses deploy.sh and fails if the build context is not backend/ or the linux/amd64 platform pin is missing.
The test derives the required runtime variable set from the backend source rather than a hardcoded list, so a new os.getenv in a service fails the build until the deploy script injects it.
The test asserts the script's service name matches the name used in the skill's verify and rollback commands.
No cloud credentials or network access are required to run it.

items.title: Coordinate-Based Maps Imagery
items.description: Delivers FR-32 and FR-33; observes NFR-15 and NFR-16.

items.title: As an analyst I can fetch attributed satellite imagery for a coordinate
items.description: DONE except one line. backend/tools/maps_imagery_service.py created and verified: validates the coordinate before spending a request, checks status AND content type AND the PNG signature and 640x640 dimensions before treating a body as an image, raises MapsImageryError, and provably never leaks the key - a forced exception carrying a fake AIzaSyFAKEKEY123 appeared in neither the log nor the raised message. One live fetch returned 334,378 bytes of 640x640 PNG. README, setup_gcp.sh and the EPIC-01 environment table all carry GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY with the restriction guidance. BLOCKED LINE: .env.example could not be updated - the editor's Copilot file-ignore rejects it even though guard_secrets.py explicitly excepts .env.(example|sample|template). Tracked by TASK-022. The missing line is 'GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY=' with a comment.
acceptance_criteria: A valid coordinate fetch produces a 640x640 satellite PNG with Google's attribution watermark intact.
A failed or non-image Maps response is rejected and is never passed to heat analysis.
The documented environment contract names GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY without disclosing its value.

items.title: As an analyst I can analyse a location without uploading an image
items.description: US-10.2; EPIC-010; FR-32 and FR-33; NFR-15. POST /api/analyze accepts one image source and returns its provenance in the saved report.
acceptance_criteria: A valid lat/lng pair without a file returns HTTP 200 with a complete saved report whose image_source is google_maps
A valid image upload continues to return a complete report whose image_source is caller
Without an upload the API requires a complete valid coordinate pair; valid uploads retain existing optional coordinate identity fields, and out-of-range coordinates return HTTP 422
A Maps fetch failure returns a generic HTTP 502 response, and a valid image-upload request remains usable

items.title: As an analyst I can choose any location in the dashboard
items.description: UI DONE, attribution NOT satisfied. Location-first mode with city shortcuts and editable lat/lng, mutually exclusive with upload mode, both provenances rendered distinctly, no key or Maps URL in the page source. GAP: POST /api/analyze returns no image and no displayable reference, so the dashboard cannot show the Maps imagery it analysed. attribution_required=true is a Google terms obligation, so this is a compliance gap, not just a demo weakness. The designer correctly refused to add a browser-side Maps call, which would have exposed the key. Folded into STORY-037 as an imagery-serving endpoint.
acceptance_criteria: The dashboard accepts latitude from -90 to 90 and longitude from -180 to 180, with existing city presets available as coordinate shortcuts.
An analyst can submit a coordinate-only analysis without selecting or uploading an image.
An uploaded image remains selectable and submit-capable in the dashboard.
The resulting report visibly distinguishes caller-uploaded imagery from Google Maps imagery.

items.title: As an operator I can protect the Maps key and conserve imagery quota
items.description: Expanded during sprint 6 to close the STORY-036 attribution gap. Original scope: protect GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY and conserve imagery quota - caching keyed on normalised coordinate plus zoom/size/maptype (never the key), proof the key reaches neither logs nor the browser, and safe failure across client, API and dashboard. ADDED scope: a backend imagery-serving route so the dashboard can display the analysed Maps image with its attribution watermark intact, keeping the key server-side. That route is also the natural place for the cache to pay off, since the analyse call and the display call hit the same coordinate.
acceptance_criteria: Browser requests contain coordinates but never GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY.
A failed Maps request leaves no key or key-bearing request URL in application logs or client-facing error responses.
Repeated requests with identical normalized imagery parameters reuse the successful image without another Maps API request.
Different imagery request parameters never receive a cached image for another coordinate or map view.

items.title: Prove attribution-required imagery is displayed by the dashboard
items.description: Sprint 6 integration exposed that coordinate analysis returned attribution_required=true without an image route, leaving the dashboard unable to display the Maps image with its required attribution. STORY-037 closed the delivery gap; this task makes the cross-layer compliance obligation an explicit regression check.
acceptance_criteria: A coordinate analysis marked attribution_required=true can be displayed in the dashboard with the Google attribution watermark intact and uncropped.
Integration coverage verifies the dashboard consumes the API-served image rather than making a browser-side Maps request or silently omitting the image.
A missing or unavailable attributed image produces an explicit user-visible error and never presents the report as if attribution were satisfied.

items.title: Require conclusive QA outcomes for long-running validation runs
items.description: Sprint 6 QA handoff returned inconclusive after a long run; the authoritative full-suite rerun established the 607-pass result. sprint_report.py already distinguishes pass, fail and timeout, but the report does not record the exact executed command or deterministic rerun instruction. Make both the run handoff and report conclusive without treating a timeout, interruption or missing result as a pass.
acceptance_criteria: A completed QA run records its final PASS or FAIL, exact executed command, and relevant summary from that execution.
A timeout, interruption, or missing result is explicitly INCONCLUSIVE with the reason and a deterministic rerun command, never PASS.
The sprint report records only an authoritative completed run, including command, verdict and summary; a timed-out or stale result is not presented as current.

items.title: Share cached Maps imagery across Cloud Run instances
items.description: Cannot be honestly completed offline: cross-instance retrieval requires shared provisioned infrastructure such as Redis/Memorystore, and process-local mocks cannot prove it. No such infrastructure or cloud quota is approved this sprint. The dashboard already handles a cache-miss HTTP 502 explicitly while keeping the valid analysis result, so this is a robustness improvement rather than a correctness defect. Keep blocked pending human approval for shared-cache infrastructure and a permitted verification approach.
acceptance_criteria: An image cached by one service instance can be retrieved by another instance using the existing analysis identifier.
Cache misses and expired entries return a safe explicit response without serving unrelated or stale image bytes.
Cross-instance display does not trigger another Maps request and preserves the original Google attribution watermark.

items.title: Bound per-instance Maps request rate
items.description: The original service-wide quota criterion cannot be met offline without a shared counter, authentication layer or gateway, and no provisioned infrastructure is approved. Re-scope this task to a local defensive budget that is fully testable with mocked Maps responses. This is explicitly a per-process bound, not service-wide spend enforcement: Cloud Run instances may each consume their own configured allowance. The true aggregate quota control remains a separate unresolved operational requirement; do not claim this task solves it.
acceptance_criteria: Each process enforces a configurable per-process limit on Maps cache-miss requests before any external call; successful cache hits do not spend the allowance.
Requests over the local limit fail with a documented generic response before the Maps call, without exposing the key or provider details.
Offline tests cover allowed requests, the limit boundary, rejection without an outbound call, and allowance reset using mocked time/client behavior; no live Maps access is used.
README documents the configuration and clearly states that per-process limits multiply across Cloud Run instances and do not enforce a service-wide spend cap.

items.title: Raise Maps imagery client coverage to the 70 percent floor
items.description: Sprint 6 report measured backend/tools/maps_imagery_service.py at 37.8%, below the project's 70% floor. Add focused offline tests for the client validation and image-response checks without making live Maps calls.
acceptance_criteria: Coverage for backend/tools/maps_imagery_service.py reaches at least 70%.
Tests cover invalid coordinates before request, provider status and content type, PNG signature, and 640x640 dimension validation.
The focused tests run offline and do not require a Maps API key or cloud access.

items.title: Verify frontend deployability and runtime configuration in release evidence
items.description: Sprint 7 retro: BUG-026 was invisible for three sprints because every container proof exercised backend/Dockerfile only; the deployed Streamlit frontend was a broken WSGI/buildpack deployment, lacked streamlit after TASK-032 split dependencies, and had no API_BASE_URL. Add an enduring frontend-specific release check so a healthy backend cannot stand in for a working dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Build and run the frontend from frontend/Dockerfile in a clean local container using the frontend dependency set; do not rely on buildpack detection.
Verify Streamlit starts, honors the injected port, and returns healthy at /_stcore/health.
Verify release configuration sets API_BASE_URL to the backend, and the deployed frontend URL completes a coordinate analysis end to end.
Record frontend and backend verification results separately in release evidence; backend-only container proof cannot satisfy frontend deployability.

items.title: Re-estimate stale-test impact when scope is added mid-sprint
items.description: Sprint 7 retro, extending rather than duplicating delivered TASK-043. The phase-4 rule was added during sprint 7, so it could not govern sprint-7 planning. Applied prospectively, it should have identified the one assertion invalidated by TASK-045's deliberate behavior change. It could not predict TASK-038's human-approved legacy-script deletion because that work was added after planning. Add a change-control step: when authorized scope is added mid-sprint, identify invalidated tests and rebaseline estimate and capacity before implementation; record exceptional human-directed work explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Before a committed behavior-changing item starts, its description names affected existing tests and includes their updates in its estimate, as required by TASK-043.
Before any human-approved or otherwise authorized scope addition starts mid-sprint, identify tests invalidated by the change and update the point estimate and sprint rebaseline.
The sprint report distinguishes committed delivery from authorized unplanned work and records the revised total; stale-test fixes are not silently absorbed.

items.title: Make container packaging acceptance independent of stale local image hashes
items.description: Sprint 7 retro: tests/test_sprint3_acceptance.py::test_hardened_image_application_sources_match_canonical_workspace compares the workspace with sources inside a locally tagged Docker image. On this machine the test required a manual docker build to refresh hotspot-hardened:latest mid-sprint; a clean checkout or CI may have no matching image, and a stale image is not evidence for current source. Replace the implicit local-image prerequisite with source-tied, reproducible evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The packaging acceptance test does not depend on a previously built local image tag or stale source hash.
A clean checkout or CI run has a deterministic path to compare current workspace source with the tested image, without a manual mid-sprint image refresh.
If Docker or a required build artifact is unavailable, the result is explicitly skipped/inconclusive and cannot be reported as a passing packaging proof.

items.title: GitHub Actions CI/CD and Release Automation
items.description: Delivers FR-34 through FR-39: establish GitHub Actions quality gates for the offline suite and coverage floor, generated dependency exports, both linux/amd64 container builds and public-repository secret scanning; protect main with required checks; then deploy validated versioned releases to Cloud Run using Workload Identity Federation. CI and build visibility are useful before the 2026-10-11 competition submission, but this epic does not block submission; branch protection and production deployment automation are post-submission work.

items.title: As a contributor I can see test and coverage results for every change
items.description: Submission-adjacent CI foundation, useful before 2026-10-11 but not a submission gate. Establishes the clean-runner quality check; account for TASK-053 first so packaging acceptance no longer depends on a pre-existing local Docker image.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow executes python3 -m pytest -o addopts='' -q on pushes and pull requests and reports the completed test result.
The coverage job uses tests/coverage.ini and fails when the configured 70% per-file floor is missed.
The test and coverage jobs run without cloud credentials or network access to application services.
The workflow caches uv dependencies with cache invalidation tied to uv.lock.

items.title: As a maintainer I can detect stale dependency exports before merge
items.description: Submission-adjacent consistency check. pyproject.toml and uv.lock remain authoritative; requirements.txt, backend/requirements.txt and frontend/requirements.txt are generated exports and must not drift silently.
acceptance_criteria: CI regenerates all three requirements exports from the authoritative project metadata and lockfile.
CI fails when a committed export differs from the generated output.
A clean export check leaves all generated files unchanged when they are current.

items.title: As an operator I can see both production images build for Cloud Run
items.description: Submission-adjacent build matrix prompted by BUG-026: backend-only container proof hid a broken deployed frontend for three sprints. Build checks depend on TASK-053 so a clean runner does not require a stale local image hash. This is build proof, not a replacement for TASK-051's separate frontend runtime and release verification.
acceptance_criteria: Push and pull-request checks build the backend with context backend and backend/Dockerfile.
Push and pull-request checks build the frontend with context frontend and frontend/Dockerfile.
Both builds explicitly target linux/amd64 and use reusable GitHub Actions Docker layer caching.
CI reports each image build independently, so one successful image cannot mask failure of the other.

items.title: As a maintainer I can catch exposed credentials before code is merged
items.description: Public-repository guard for pushes and pull requests. Findings must be safe to report: detected credential values are never written to workflow logs, and scanning must not require cloud credentials.
acceptance_criteria: The secret scan runs on pushes and pull requests, including pull requests from forks.
A detected secret produces a failing, visible status check without exposing the secret value in logs or annotations.
The scan runs without GitHub secrets or Google Cloud credentials, including for fork pull requests.

items.title: As a maintainer I can prevent merges when required GitHub checks fail
items.description: Post-submission repository-governance work. Configure a GitHub ruleset for main after the CI and secret-scan check names are stable; this is a repository setting, not a workflow-file substitute.
acceptance_criteria: The main-branch ruleset requires the designated CI and secret-scan checks before merge.
A pull request cannot merge when either required check is failing or has not completed.
The ruleset applies to main and is visible in the public repository settings.

items.title: As an operator I can deploy a verified release to Cloud Run without key files
items.description: Post-submission only; current manual deployment remains the submission path. Do not enable until TASK-048's deploy-script findings are corrected, TASK-051 proves frontend runtime/release verification, and TASK-053 removes local-image-hash dependence. Use manually created vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tags as release identifiers; automated semantic version calculation and changelog generation are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Deployment runs only for a vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release tag whose commit is on main and whose required CI and secret-scan checks passed; pull-request events never deploy.
The workflow authenticates to Google Cloud with Workload Identity Federation and creates or uses no service-account key file.
The workflow deploys both linux/amd64 images to hotspot-backend and hotspot-frontend in asia-southeast1, preserving the backend's BIGQUERY_LOCATION=US exception and required runtime configuration.
Release evidence reports backend and frontend verification separately, including backend health and frontend health plus a coordinate-analysis check.
Fork pull requests receive no GitHub secrets or cloud credentials, and workflow logs contain no secret values.
